subject: SpringLight Health — residency & private hosting alignment (post-call)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@springlight.health>, Emily Torres <emily.torres@springlight.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: SpringLight host residency & private hosting alignment — post-call notes

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain / drivers you shared:
- Regulatory: multiple payer contracts require data to remain in US-only regions; potential state-level restrictions for PHI.
- Air-gap requirement: Q3 pilots may need an air-gapped on-prem option for a subset of workloads (audit-driven).
- Network constraints: strict egress limitations and a single outbound NAT; no inbound public IPs permitted.
- Ops: limited internal NetOps headcount; prefer templated checklists and a clear handoff for configuration.

Goals we agreed on:
1) Confirm feasibility for a VPC-private deployment that keeps customer data in your AWS US-East accounts.
2) Determine minimum network changes required for our connector and a non-internet-facing control plane path (mutual TLS + proxying through your jump host).
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your NetOps + Security to validate firewall rules, routing, and any burden for managed key material.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
- Redwood to share a concise network checklist + an initial topology sketch — Naomi (today EOD) — attached: springlight-network-topology-draft.pdf
- NetOps deep-dive (30–45m): target week of 6/10 — owner: Amit to confirm available slots
- Provide SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM integration notes: Ben (by 6/3) — attachment: soc2-evidence-pack-stub.zip
- Draft mutual action plan / rough timeline for pilot (incl. on-prem air-gap path): Marissa (by 6/5)

Attachments: springlight-network-topology-draft.pdf (sketch), redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx (template), SOC2 evidence stub.

If that matches your read, reply with preferred times for the NetOps deep-dive and any immediate blockers we missed.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
From: Amit Shah <amit.shah@springlight.health>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Torres <emily.torres@springlight.health>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-01T19:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SpringLight host residency & private hosting alignment — post-call notes

Thanks Naomi — this is great and captures the call.

Quick clarifications:
- For the air-gap pilot we expect the dataset to be scrubbed / deidentified before transit; will need a runbook for data ingestion pre-flight.
- Our NetOps prefers outbound-only connections over a dedicated proxy; inbound mTLS endpoints are unlikely to be approved without an architecture exception.

Amit will loop in our security ops (secops@springlight.health) for the deep-dive. For availability: 6/11 between 13:00–15:00 EDT works for our team.

Please include the checklist and SOC2 artifacts in the drive link and we'll do a quick internal review prior to the technical call.

—Amit
Amit Shah
Director, Infrastructure | SpringLight Health
amit.shah@springlight.health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@springlight.health>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-02T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SpringLight — follow-up & artifacts

Appreciate the quick reply Amit.

Notes from our side addressing the clarifications:
- We can support an outbound-only model via a persistent TLS tunnel originated from your VPC to a private Redwood egress endpoint in US-East. That avoids inbound public IPs and aligns with your proxy preference.
- For the air-gapped pilot, we'll provide a sanitized ingestion runbook and an import tool that runs behind your firewall — Marissa will own the runbook draft.
- Attached is the initial checklist (redwood-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx). I'll also drop the SOC2 evidence stub into the shared drive now.

I'll schedule the NetOps deep-dive for 6/11 13:30 EDT and send a calendar invite to the addresses on this thread unless someone objects.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@springlight.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, SecureCloud Inc. <secops@securecloud.com>
Date: 2029-06-03T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: SpringLight — NetOps deep-dive confirmed (6/11 13:30 EDT)

Thanks — invite sent for 6/11 13:30–14:15 EDT (30–45m). Agenda below and items to review ahead of time:

Agenda:
- 5m introductions & scope
- 10m network topology & egress-only tunnel approach (Ben)
- 15m key exchange / KMS/HSM integration patterns (Naomi + Marissa)
- 10m air-gap pilot ingestion runbook review (Marissa)
- 5m next steps & owners

Pre-work for attendees:
- NetOps: confirm if a jump host/proxy exists and whether you have an outbound NAT IP range we should expect.
- Security: please flag any PKI or attestation requirements prior to the call.

Deliverables we'll produce after the call:
- Finalized network diagram with exact ports/IPs (Naomi) — expected 6/14
- Pilot action plan + SOW checklist (Marissa) — expected 6/18
- HubSpot update & deal stage moved to 'Technical Validation' (Ben) — immediate

Let us know if you'd like a purely written MOP instead of a call — happy to adapt.

Thanks again, looking forward to the deep-dive.

Naomi
